accelerationist.belief: Some data leaks are physically irreversible, so liability-after-the-fact cannot restore the status quo.
accelerationist.desire: To keep intervention narrow and targeted only at the genuinely irreversible cases rather than blanketing all data flows.
accelerationist.intention: Reserve hard ex-ante controls exclusively for the small class of non-compensable harms and let markets handle the reversible rest.
accelerationist.summary: Irreversibility is the rare trigger justifying pre-emptive limits without choking off ordinary data-driven innovation.

safetyist.belief: Irreversible harms structurally exceed what tort or documentation regimes can address, leaving victims permanently uncompensated.
safetyist.desire: To prevent the harm from occurring at all through binding pre-deployment safeguards.
safetyist.intention: Mandate ex-ante prevention and hard containment for any pipeline that can touch non-compensable data categories.
safetyist.summary: Because you cannot un-leak a genome, only prevention counts as protection for irreversible harms.

skeptic.belief: Compliance regimes routinely paper over irreversible harms with documentation that changes nothing for the victim.
skeptic.desire: To expose the gap between the appearance of a remedy and the reality that nothing was actually restored.
skeptic.intention: Refuse to accept records or payments as remedies and force scrutiny onto whether harm was actually preventable.
skeptic.summary: A documented record of an irreversible leak is a governance mirage, not a remedy.

cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: No existing node captures the specific claim that irreversibility categorically defeats post-hoc remedies. 'What Does AI Harm Mean' and 'Data-Driven Harms' are too general; this is about the temporal/reversibility structure of the harm defeating remedy design.

cross_cutting_proposals.agreement_text: The party sued owns the logs, model internals, and interaction traces that would prove a leak, so standing to sue is empty without an evidence rail that forces the proof into the open.
cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: This is exactly the 'Privatization of Proof' node — the defendant controls the evidence needed to prove liability against them, hollowing out standing without a forced-disclosure evidence rail.

cross_cutting_proposals.agreement_text: The standard-setting body must be structurally separated from the party profiting from the data flow — externally set and publicly funded — because self-defined standards get narrowed rather than enforced.
cross_cutting_proposals.proposed_description: A situation within AI policy discourse that concerns whether the body defining privacy/safety standards must be structurally and financially separated from the parties that profit from the regulated data flows. Encompasses: publicly funded external standard-setting, capture-resistance in norm definition, and the tendency of self-defined standards toward narrowing. Excludes: the legitimacy of the standardization process itself (throughput legitimacy) and who enforces once standards exist.

accelerationist.belief: Self-defined standards get narrowed to whatever incumbents already do, freezing the field around current practice.
accelerationist.desire: To keep standards from being weaponized as a moat that entrenches large data-profiting incumbents.
accelerationist.intention: Push standard-setting authority to an externally funded body insulated from the largest players' commercial interests.
accelerationist.summary: External standard-setters prevent incumbents from writing the rules into a competitive moat.

safetyist.belief: Parties profiting from a data flow will define standards to minimize their own obligations, not to protect the public.
safetyist.desire: To ensure protective standards are genuinely binding rather than self-serving minimums.
safetyist.intention: Establish publicly funded, independent standard bodies with authority to set and revise protective floors.
safetyist.summary: Only a body without financial stake in the data flow will set standards that actually protect people.

skeptic.belief: Standard-setting captured by profit-takers reliably degrades into compliance theater rather than enforcement.
skeptic.desire: To break the conflict of interest that turns standards into narrowed, unenforced formalities.
skeptic.intention: Demand structural separation and public funding as a precondition before treating any standard as credible.
skeptic.summary: Standards defined by the profiting party are captured by design and collapse into unenforced narrowing.

cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: Existing nodes 'Standardisation as Law-Making' and 'Throughput Legitimacy in Standardisation' address the process and legitimacy of standardization but not the specific structural-independence/capture claim about separating the standard-setter from the profiting party. This is a distinct contested concept.

cross_cutting_proposals.agreement_text: The delegation-edge disclosure floor — recording which agent directed the next to act, on whose authority, at what timestamp — is the enforcement rail that makes accountability fire across a multi-vendor orchestration chain; the Accelerationist calls the Skeptic's object-keyed reconciled ledger 'the enforcement rail I want, not a rival to it.'
cross_cutting_proposals.proposed_description: A situation within AI policy discourse that concerns the minimum mandatory record — which agent directed which next agent to act, on whose authority, and when — needed to make accountability enforceable across a multi-vendor agent orchestration chain. Encompasses: delegation-edge logging, object-keyed reconciled ledgers, and cross-vendor attribution of agentic actions. Excludes: the general disclosure-of-agency question (whether a user knows they face an agent) and the reliability of provenance attestations against determined evaders.

accelerationist.belief: A lightweight per-edge record of who directed whom is sufficient to route accountability without slowing orchestration.
accelerationist.desire: To enable multi-vendor agent ecosystems to scale while keeping liability attributable at the specific delegation edge.
accelerationist.intention: Adopt the object-keyed ledger as a shared, low-friction enforcement rail rather than a competing regulatory burden.
accelerationist.summary: The delegation-edge log is the enforcement rail I want — accountability that fires without a compliance drag on scaling.

safetyist.belief: Without a record of each delegation handoff, harms in a multi-vendor chain become unattributable and no party is held responsible.
safetyist.desire: To guarantee that accountability reaches every actor in an orchestration chain, not just the last visible one.
safetyist.intention: Mandate the delegation-edge disclosure floor as a binding requirement for any multi-agent deployment.
safetyist.summary: A mandatory delegation-edge floor is what makes accountability actually fire across the whole chain.

skeptic.belief: Standing and liability are hollow across vendor chains unless the reconciled ledger forces attribution into the open.
skeptic.desire: To close the diffusion-of-responsibility gap where multi-vendor orchestration launders accountability.
skeptic.intention: Insist on an object-keyed reconciled ledger as the concrete mechanism that prevents accountability from evaporating between vendors.
skeptic.summary: The object-keyed reconciled ledger is the rail that stops multi-vendor chains from laundering responsibility.

cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: While 'Human-AI Operational Configuration Tracking,' 'Disclosure Problem in AI Agency,' and 'Intent-Graph Problem in Agentic AI' are adjacent, none captures the specific convergent-mechanism claim of a delegation-edge disclosure floor / object-keyed reconciled ledger as the shared enforcement rail. The rare cross-POV endorsement of one concrete mechanism warrants its own node.

cross_cutting_proposals.agreement_text: The cross-border enforcement problem wounds every proposed instrument equally — a domestic judgment against a judgment-proof or offshore-orchestrated actor and a halt order that cannot reach an offshore vendor are both unenforceable — so it is a shared blind spot rather than an asymmetric weakness of any one design.
cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: This maps to the existing 'Cross-Border Enforcement Reach as Precondition for Distribution-Stage Liability' node, which addresses the unenforceability of instruments against offshore/judgment-proof actors as a shared constraint on all liability designs.
cross_cutting_proposals.maps_to_existing: Cross-Border Enforcement Reach as Precondition for Distribution-Stage Liability

cross_cutting_proposals.agreement_text: A signed provenance record is a proxy: it attests to what a vendor chose to record, not what an out-of-band pipeline actually ingested, so any attestation-based rail can be defeated by a determined evader who redefines or offshores the ingestion point.
cross_cutting_proposals.proposed_description: A situation within AI policy discourse that concerns the gap between a signed provenance attestation (what a vendor chose to record) and the actual data ingestion (what an out-of-band or offshored pipeline really consumed), and how determined evaders defeat attestation-based rails by relocating or redefining the ingestion point. Encompasses: provenance-record spoofing, out-of-band ingestion, and the evasion ceiling of any attestation mechanism. Excludes: cross-border enforcement of judgments generally, and the delegation-edge accountability rail for agent actions.

accelerationist.belief: Attestation rails only bind honest actors; determined evaders redefine the ingestion point and slip past them anyway.
accelerationist.desire: To avoid imposing heavy attestation mandates that burden compliant firms while failing to catch the actual bad actors.
accelerationist.intention: Treat attestation as a low-cost signal for good-faith actors rather than a load-bearing enforcement guarantee.
accelerationist.summary: Attestation catches only the honest; evaders offshore the ingestion point, so don't overbuild on a defeatable proxy.

safetyist.belief: A provenance record proves only what was recorded, leaving a structural blind spot for out-of-band ingestion.
safetyist.desire: To close the gap so that data provenance guarantees actually track real ingestion rather than self-report.
safetyist.intention: Supplement attestation with independent verification and ingestion-point controls so the proxy cannot be quietly bypassed.
safetyist.summary: A provenance attestation is only a proxy; without verifying actual ingestion the safeguard has a built-in blind spot.

skeptic.belief: Signed provenance is a self-serving artifact attesting to a vendor's chosen record, not to reality.
skeptic.desire: To expose attestation-based governance as defeatable theater rather than genuine assurance.
skeptic.intention: Refuse to treat provenance records as proof and demand mechanisms that observe the actual ingestion point.
skeptic.summary: A provenance signature attests to what the vendor recorded, not what was ingested — a defeatable proxy dressed as proof.

cross_cutting_proposals.rationale: Existing nodes 'AI Provenance and Latent Manifests,' 'Anchoring Data-Provenance Liability at the In-Jurisdiction Deployment Act,' and 'Supervisability Evasion' touch nearby, but none captures the specific epistemic claim that a signed provenance record is a defeatable proxy for actual ingestion. This is the distinct 'attestation proves only what was recorded' concept.
